acceptance_criteria.text: The Event Organiser who owns the event can submit a change request while the event is Approved, Planning, Safety review, Safety approved, Confirmed or Postponed; a change request cannot be submitted in any other status. A request can propose new values for any field the Coordinator can edit in Update Event Information (SPM-62): title, category, purpose, description, start and end date and time, expected attendance, preferred layout, required facilities, accessibility notes and special requirements. Changes to equipment are described in free text.
The request lists each field being changed, with its current value and the proposed value.
The Event Organiser must give a reason for the change; a request without a reason is refused.

Given a request changes the date and time, expected attendance, venue requirements (preferred layout or required facilities) or equipment, when the assigned Event Coordinator views their pending change requests, then the request is marked Important; a request that changes only other fields is not marked.

The Event Organiser can request that the event be postponed or cancelled; the request is processed by the assigned Coordinator (see: Postpone Event, Cancel Event) and does not change the event's status by itself.
The original event arrangements remain unchanged until the request is processed.

test_cases.title: The owning organiser requests new details for an Approved event, and the event lists the request with each field's current and proposed value while its own details stay the same
test_cases.preconditions: Run npm run fixtures:spm35 before and after this case (it saves a change request). 'SPM35 Harbour Townhall' is Approved, organised by Rachel Ng (Meridian Financial Group), coordinator Daniel Tan, 12 Apr 2027, 09:00–12:00, with no change requests. Logged in as rachel.ng@meridianfina.com / password123 (Event Organiser).
steps: Click 'My Events' in the sidebar and open 'SPM35 Harbour Townhall'
Click 'Request a change'
Change 'Event name' to 'SPM35 Harbour Townhall and Awards'
Change 'Description' to 'Leadership update, Q&A and the staff awards.'
Enter the reason in 'Reason for the change'
Click 'Send change request'
Click 'Back to event'
test_cases.test_data:
Event: SPM35 Harbour Townhall (Approved)
Event name: SPM35 Harbour Townhall -> SPM35 Harbour Townhall and Awards
Description: Leadership update and Q&A. -> Leadership update, Q&A and the staff awards.
Reason for the change: We are presenting the staff awards at the townhall.
test_cases.expected_result:
Step 1: The event page shows the 'Approved' status badge and a 'Request a change' button.
Step 2: The 'Request a change' page opens with 'What do you need?' set to 'Change the event's details', the event's current details filled in, an 'Equipment changes' box and a required 'Reason for the change' box.
Step 6: A green alert 'Change request sent to your coordinator.' reads 'Nothing about the event changes until your coordinator processes the request.'
Step 7: The event page still shows the title 'SPM35 Harbour Townhall' and the 'Approved' status badge. A 'Change requests' card lists one 'Change of details' request with the badge 'Pending' and no 'Important' badge, 'Requested by Rachel Ng on' today's date, 'Reason: We are presenting the staff awards at the townhall.', and a table of Field, Current and Proposed with two rows: 'Event name' 'SPM35 Harbour Townhall' -> 'SPM35 Harbour Townhall and Awards', and 'Description' 'Leadership update and Q&A.' -> 'Leadership update, Q&A and the staff awards.'

open_questions: DECIDED 2026-10-20: the organiser's way in is a 'Request a change' button in the event page header, shown only to the organiser who owns the event while it is Approved, Planning, Safety review, Safety approved, Confirmed or Postponed. The page is 'Request a change' at /events/<reference>/change-request (UI_DESIGN.md S-10). Anyone else who types the address sees 'You can't request a change to this event' with 'Only the organiser who owns this event can request a change.' or 'A change can only be requested while the event is Approved, Planning, Safety review, Safety approved, Confirmed or Postponed.'

DECIDED 2026-10-20: the form asks 'What do you need?' - 'Change the event's details' (the default), 'Postpone the event' or 'Cancel the event'. The details use the same labels, sections and rules as Edit event information (SPM-62), filled in with the event's current values; only the fields changed are sent. Below them, 'Equipment changes' (free text, AC1). Every kind needs 'Reason for the change' (AC3). Buttons: 'Send change request' and 'Back to event' (not 'Cancel', which would read as cancelling the event).

DECIDED 2026-10-20: messages. Missing reason: 'Give a reason for the change.' A change of details with nothing changed and no equipment text: 'Change at least one detail, or describe the equipment change.' (UI_DESIGN.md S-10: 'At least one proposed change required'). Sent: 'Change request sent to your coordinator.' with 'Nothing about the event changes until your coordinator processes the request.' Postpone and cancel notes: 'Your coordinator decides whether to postpone the event. It stays <status> until then.' / '... whether to cancel the event. ...'

DECIDED 2026-10-20: the requests are shown on the event's Overview in a 'Change requests' card (newest first) to the event's organisers, its assigned coordinator and the Ops Manager, and to the coordinator on a new 'Change Requests' sidebar page (/change-requests) listing the pending requests on the events assigned to them, newest first. Each shows the kind ('Change of details', 'Postponement', 'Cancellation'), the status badge, 'Important' where it applies with 'Affects existing arrangements: <labels>.', 'Requested by <name> on <date, time>', 'Reason: …', a Field / Current / Proposed table and 'Equipment: …'. The organiser sees the 'Important' badge too.

DECIDED 2026-10-20: 'Important' (AC4) is IMPORTANT_CHANGES from SPM-62 (src/lib/eventChangeImpact.ts): the date and time, expected attendance, venue requirements (preferred layout or the facilities, including accessibility needs, the venue must have) and equipment (any text in 'Equipment changes'). A postponement or cancellation request changes no field, so it is not marked Important.

DECIDED 2026-10-20: a postponement request carries a reason only. A new date the organiser already knows is a change of details (new Starts at / Ends at), which customer clarification #69 treats as a rescheduling request.

DECIDED 2026-10-20: each request stores, per field, the value it had when the request was made and the value proposed, so the request still shows what it asked for if the event changes later. The facilities are stored with their names. Process Event Change Request (SPM-32) reads the proposed values in the same shape as Update Event Information's payload.

DECIDED 2026-10-20: a multi-session event's times, attendance and layout come from its sessions, which Edit event information cannot change yet (SPM-62), so the request form cannot propose them either; it says 'Session times and attendance can't be changed here yet - describe the change in Reason for the change.' Covered by unit tests only: no SPM-35 fixture event has sessions.
DECIDED 2026-10-20: an organiser may have more than one pending request on the same event. Nothing in the story limits it, and SPM-32 decides each one.

DECIDED 2026-10-20: requests made before SPM-35 (three in the base seed) have only a proposed start, end or attendance. They are shown from those values, with the event's present value as Current, and keep their stored significance as Important.
RESOLVED 2026-10-20: notifying the coordinator of a new request is not in this story - it was removed from the ACs and belongs to Receive Event Notifications (SPM-53). No case for it.

RESOLVED 2026-10-20: approving, rejecting or partly approving a request, and any change it makes to the event or its arrangements, is Process Event Change Request (SPM-32), Postpone Event and Cancel Event. This story only records the request. No case for it.
